# Security policy

TenantFence is an early 0.1 release. Use the latest source and review the documented limitations before testing. Only run with explicit authorization and disposable fixtures.

For vulnerabilities in TenantFence itself, use this repository's GitHub **Security → Advisories → Report a vulnerability** private reporting feature if enabled. If unavailable, contact the maintainer through a private contact method listed on their GitHub profile. Do not post credentials, private customer data or a working exploit in a public issue. No dedicated response-time guarantee or fabricated security email address is provided.

Include the affected revision, impact, sanitized reproduction and synthetic fixtures. The deliberately vulnerable local lab is documented intentional behavior; a way to reach it through the normal secure deployment graph or bypass its local-only controls is a security issue.

Findings in third-party APIs belong in those projects' disclosure processes. See docs/security.md for the tool's threat model and data-handling behavior.
